title.narrative: Supporting Sudan Educational System in ESD, GCED-PVE

description.narrative: Background: Despite wide variations among and within countries especially between public and quality private schools, the context of GCE in most Arab public schools does not support the development of global citizenship values. The school climate is generally authoritarian and repressive. Good governance, particularly accountability and transparency, is rare. Learning methods and practices are largely limited to rote instruction. Lessons tend to be didactic and teacher-directed rather than student-centred. Arab countries have diverse priorities in their education policies, and GCE is not among them. One group seeks to raise religious citizens as its highest priority; another, patriotic nationalists; and a third group desires to graduate youth with two or more identities—ethnic, religious, national, and regional. Tunisia is unique in emphasizing the global dimension of citizenship. Most Arab public schools offer limited opportunities for students to put lessons into practice. And limited extracurricular activities inside and outside schools deprive students of actual global citizenship experiences, thus hindering the development of their global citizenship knowledge, skills, values and behaviour. GCE in the Arab countries faces six main challenges: (1) shortcomings of education systems (weak governance and poor preparation of teachers both academically and pedagogically); (2) domestic context (resistance from some social and cultural groups); (3) international context (shortcomings in Western foreign policies regarding Arabs); (4) political and social commitment; (5) funding, and (6) conflict between the national and global dimensions of citizenship identity. The issue of Global Citizenship Education (GCED) is one of UNESCO Khartoum focus areas in education, with the support of Beirut regional office senior Sudanese education specialists and officials participated in regional and local activities in the past. Sudan, emerging from the previous political regime and venturing in the transitional period needs to strengthen capacities in these values. After revolution in Sudan a third national education conference was convened to draw the lines of the future of education in Sudan and address many urgent problems facing education in Sudan. One of the main topics was the national curricula, the main recommendation was to change radically the national curricula to match with current needs of the Sudanese public and international standards. This curriculum change is a crucial moment if well managed can integrate GCED values into the future curricula, the Secretary General of the National Centre for Curriculum Development and Educational Research believes UNESCO should continue to support this important change in curricula. Sudan is currently revising its educational curricula for both, formal and non-formal education. For formal education, first 4 steps are already finished (for children of 6-9 years). Without immediate support for bringing new education ideas into the curricula, the Sudanese educators will revise the curricula up to their knowledge and experience – continuing the current (obsolete) way of doing things. Previous curricula revision took place in 1992. Teacher training is also undergoing dramatic changes with the establishment of the National Center for Teacher Training. It is important to note that teacher’s training programs (pre and in-service) are currently also been reviewed, this provide an additional opportunity to integrate ESD and Global Citizenship issues in future training manuals. This project aims at enhancing the Sudan education system on issues related to the ESD and GCED-PVE, building on previous efforts with the National Center for Curricula Development and Educational Research Outcome N° 1: Sudanese National Education systems are equipped to promote ESD and GCED-PVE. Output N°1: Sudan national capacities are developed to integrate GCED and ESD. Act. 1 Enhance and develop a National Curricula Matrix and a Teacher’s Guide on GCED in close collaboration with national and international educational experts and MoE and the NCCDER. Implementation strategy: This will be achieved through supporting the curricula developers to integrate value and attitudes relevant to ESD, CGED and PVE. This will be mainly achieved through capacity building on curricula developers developing the new books of Sudan.
